title: Stream continuity negotiation and fragment handoff for resilient SSE streaming
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a resilient SSE streaming layer that supports graceful fragment handoff between serving workers, a lightweight continuity negotiation handshake for clients, and compatibility shims for older chunk-id-based clients. The goal is to minimize token re-generation on reconnects, preserve function-call/structured-output boundaries across handoffs, and provide clear metrics and observability for resume success rates. This ticket covers protocol design, server implementation changes (handoff markers + soft-state resume tokens), client-facing compatibility headers, and an automated test harness for reconnect scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can reconnect after an ephemeral worker restart and resume a stream with <= 2 tokens of duplication in 99% of synthetic reconnect tests

Function call frames (structured outputs) are not split across resumed segments: resumed stream replays any incomplete function-call frame as a single re-emitted boundary or signals a deterministic rewind to the last safe boundary
Backward compatibility header X-RI-Chunk-Compat toggles legacy chunk-id resume behavior for older clients; new default uses Continuity Token negotiation
Fragment handoff is implemented such that ownership transfer between workers does not require client-side changes and adds <1ms median extra latency for in-flight token emission
End-to-end integration tests covering: worker preemption, network flapping, delayed fragment arrival, and cross-zone handoffs are added and pass in CI
Dashboard panels added for resume-success-rate, average replayed-tokens-per-resume, and fragment-handoff-rate; alerts configured for >1% resume failure over 10m
design_decisions: Use a soft-state Continuity Token (base64) containing a compact sequence window and a checksum instead of exposing raw offsets to clients
A two-way negotiation: client sends last-seen token in reconnect handshake; server validates and either accepts (resume) or responds with a deterministic fallback point and reason
Introduce an internal handoff marker (HND-<seq>) appended to fragment envelopes that workers can emit to identify in-flight handoff boundaries without altering user-visible payloads

To protect function-call atomicity, the runtime will treat any fragment that contains a function-call start without a corresponding function-call end as an unsafe boundary and will rewind to the last safe frame on resume

Legacy support: if X-RI-Chunk-Compat: 1 is present, the server will attempt to reconcile using per-chunk ids and a best-effort replay mode; this mode is opt-in and not eligible for SLA-backed resume guarantees
implementation_notes: Server: extend existing fragment envelope with fields: continuity_token (opaque), handoff_marker (HND-<seq>), and optional provenance header for worker_id

Worker handoff flow: origin worker emits final fragment with handoff_marker and registers the token in a shared faststore (redis with TTL=1m); new owner verifies and claims the token before emitting further fragments

Reconnect handshake: POST /v1/streams/:id/reconnect with body {last_seen_token: "..."}; response 200 {resume: true, server_token: "..."} or 409 {resume: false, fallback_token: "...", reason: "handoff_mismatch"}
Function-call handling: add fc_id per function-call boundary inside fragment metadata; on resume, if fc_id is open, server will re-emit a close frame or rewind to safe boundary depending on policy
Compatibility shim: X-RI-Chunk-Compat toggles parsing of chunk_id header and engages older resume path; warn in logs when engaged
Observability: emit metrics: resume_attempt, resume_success, resumed_replayed_tokens, handoff_claim_latency, handoff_failures; tag by project, model, region
Testing: extend chaos harness to preempt worker after sending partial fragment, simulate client reconnect with different tokens, and verify deterministic outcomes
Docs: update streaming API reference with reconnect examples for new clients and a migration guide for chunk-id clients
notes: Initial spike found a race when origin worker cleaned its local cache before registering token in faststore — fixed by ordering commit before cache prune (see PR #4892)
We debated exposing absolute byte offsets vs opaque tokens; chose opaque tokens to avoid leaking internal buffer layout and to make future changes backwards-incompatible-safe
Design reviewed with PM and DX (Priya) on 2026-02-18; agreed to include explicit function-call ATOMICITY section in docs
Security: continuity tokens are not secrets but include a MAC to prevent tampering; KMS signing was considered but deferred (low-risk and higher latency)
